function: Convolution-Transformer ECT-Net predicts the next-instant ISAC transmit beamforming matrix from the previous echoes and beamformer, maximizing communication sum rate under a sensing SINR constraint (pp. 5-8).
system: mmWave massive-MIMO RSU, Nt=64 transmit and Nr=16 receive antennas on separate full-duplex ULAs, K=12 single-antenna vehicles, LOS channel, 30 GHz; no RIS (pp. 3, 9-10).
method: Two CNN modules plus attention encoder with residual link (ECT-Net), trained offline unsupervised with a penalty loss, validated, then used for online prediction (pp. 6-9).
data_channel: Own simulation: LOS mmWave channel, path-loss exponent 2.55, kinematic vehicle motion (20 m/s, 0.1 s); 2000 samples split 8:1:1 into training, validation, testing (pp. 4-5, 10).
test_conditions: Test on held-out 10% of the same simulated data (200 samples); sweeps over power, antennas 8-36, vehicles, speed, noise, road distance; no train/test mismatch stated (pp. 10-13).
baselines: Non-learned: random beamforming. Learned: HCL-Net convolutional LSTM [27]. Noise-free upper bound is the proposed network without noise; plain Transformer only in complexity table (pp. 10-11).
metrics: Average achievable communication sum rate (bits/s/Hz), average minimum sensing SINR, parameters, FLOPs, FPS, training epochs (pp. 10-14).
complexity: Big-O orders of offline training and online prediction (Eqs. 21-22); ECT-Net 0.10M parameters, 2.70M FLOPs, 930.7 FPS versus HCL-Net 0.86M, 1.12M, 422.6 (pp. 9, 11).
q1_support: p. 4: "a line-of-sight (LOS) channel is employed [34]"; own LOS model with path-loss exponent 2.55 (Table II, p. 10), no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 10: "each simulation result is the average of 200 samples run on the test set"; a held-out part of the same data, and the sweeps over power, antennas, noise and distance (pp. 11-13) never state a different training condition.
q3_support: p. 10: "convolutional LSTM network (HCL-Net) for predictive beamforming [27]" is the earlier learned baseline and "The random beamforming scheme is utilized" the non-learned one; both compared on sum rate (Fig. 6).
q4_support: p. 11: "in terms of parameters, FlOPs, and FPS"; Table III gives ECT-Net 0.10M parameters and 2.70M FLOPs, and Eqs. 21-22 (p. 9) give the Big-O orders.
q5_support: p. 10: "data sets is 2000, divided into the training set"; data come from the authors' own simulation, with no code or data link and no public dataset.
notes: Title and DOI on p. 1 match. Beamforming for ISAC from echoes, so area 5. q3: the noise-free upper bound is a variant of the proposed network, and the plain Transformer [29] appears only in the complexity table (Table III), so HCL-Net [27] and random beamforming carry the criterion. q2: the ECT-Net input and output sizes change with the antenna number (p. 8), and no train/test mismatch is stated for any sweep.
